text: My name is Manos. I'm the co founder of WeatherXM. We are deploying weather stations all around the world. We collect data, we produce better forecasts, better weather services that we give to companies that depend on weather. We're here in Mombasa, Kenya. We came here to interact with the local communities, with lawyers, with individuals, and figure out their problems and help them expand the network. We realized when we came here that the crypto rewards generated by a weather station is enough to power the electricity of a small house or a school on a daily basis. We have about 1,000 stations in Africa and another thousand in India and four or five hundred in Latin America. We monitor temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed, direction and precipitation. We use blockchain technology in our project to ensure that the stations are really where they're supposed to be on Earth and they produce the data that they claim to produce. So we have cryptographic proofs on chain. It unlocks new use cases utilizing weather data on chain, for example, to power parametric weather insurance industry or prediction markets or weather derivatives. The largest meteorological organization, NOAA in the US operates 14,000 weather stations. And we already are near 10,000 stations. And we've built that network in just two years. We do special projects in Solana. It's additional incentives to expand the network to the direction that we want. And that's how the network was established here in Nairobi, in Kenya. Solana is doing an amazing job. They are expanding the crypto adoption. So we're happy that we're part of this ecosystem. It.
